top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Grossman, citation confined to the political economy of trade protection) has the cleanest attribution on the slate. It is a long, tightly coupled two-person programme, so no one at the same level is arbitrarily excluded. The protection-for-sale framework made lobbying and tariff formation a tractable equilibrium object and has been extended, tested and criticised for about thirty years, so maturity is not in doubt. The main reservation is that the empirical support for its specific predictions is mixed. That argues for a narrow citation that does not claim confirmation, and I do not think it disqualifies the award. P002 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) is a strong, design-based contribution, but the long-run persistence and shift-share identification are still being revised and the task-framework antecedents are uncredited. P003 (Melitz, Helpman) has dense empirical confrontation but an unresolved attribution gap (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum) and rests heavily on one 2003 paper. I rank all three above no award, because each is a substantial, mature contribution.
